# Theme 2: Data Preparation & Understanding {.unnumbered}

<!-- This file is the source of a page on the course website. Read it there: https://ai.buas.nl/open-courses/introduction-to-ml/self-study/theme-2/00_overview.html -->

In Theme 1 you trained models on datasets that were ready to use, and in the End-to-End ML Project you went through all stages of a project once. Real data is rarely ready to use. In this theme you study the two data stages in depth: preparing the data and exploring it. Then you look at a question that decides whether a model works in practice: does your data look like the data the model will be used on?

Data Preparation comes before Data Understanding in this theme, the other way around from CRISP-DM. To understand a dataset, you often have to prepare it first, for example scale features before you compare them. The [End-to-End ML Project](../theme-1/06_end_to_end_ml.ipynb) explains this order in more detail.

## Activities

Work through the activities in order:

1. [Data Preparation](01_data_prep.ipynb): scaling, transforming, merging and encoding data, and handling missing values.
2. [Data Understanding](02_data_understanding.ipynb): distributions, relationships between variables, and principal component analysis (PCA).
3. [Leakage & Distribution Shift](03_leakage_and_distribution_shift.qmd): what a dataset represents, data unlike the training data, data from different sources, leakage, and how to make your development data match the data a model will be used on.

In the next Self-study theme, [Theme 3](../theme-3/00_overview.qmd), you learn to evaluate and compare models, and you look inside three of them.
